Oct 1 (Reuters) - Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier on Thursday filed ​a lawsuit against Pfizer

(PFE.N), opens new tab

and its CEO, Albert Bourla, ‌accusing the drugmaker of misleading consumers about the safety and effectiveness of its COVID-19 vaccine.

Here are more details:

Sign up here.

  • Uthmeier filed the lawsuit in state court, ​alleging that Pfizer told consumers its COVID-19 vaccine was safe ​while failing to disclose potential risks, including heart inflammation ⁠and other adverse events.

  • Pfizer, according to the lawsuit, urged people ​to get the shot to protect others, even though the company ​never tested whether the vaccine stopped the virus from spreading.

  • Florida has also accused Pfizer of using unfair tactics to dominate the market.

  • It said the company ​made more than $80 billion from vaccine sales, then nearly quadrupled ​the price of the vaccine to $110 to $130 a dose in 2023 from $30.

  • The state, ‌suing ⁠under its consumer protection law, wants a court order to stop the alleged conduct, fines of $10,000 per violation, or $15,000 when seniors or disabled people were harmed, and the return of profits.

  • Pfizer said ​in a statement ​the state's allegations ⁠have no merit and that it would respond to the suit in due course.

  • "The representations made ​by Pfizer about its COVID-19 vaccine have been ​accurate and ⁠science-based, and the company stands behind the safety and efficacy of its vaccine," the company said.

  • "The complaint and comments by Florida Attorney ⁠General ​James Uthmeier speak for themselves," the Florida ​Attorney General's Office said in response to a Reuters request for additional comment.
